generator.program.note: The program the authors chose to grow this taxon's graminoid species (named in each species' spec until G2.3a moved it here).

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Watson and Dallwitz's description of the family: the leaves are alternate.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Watson and Dallwitz's description of the family: the leaves are distichous, in two ranks.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 1934), family 384 Typhaceae: marsh or lake herbs from creeping rhizomes; leaves mostly from the base, long and linear; flowers unisexual, very many, crowded on a terminal spike (his spadix), the male above the female on the same plant. APG adds the bur-reeds (Sparganium), also herbs of wet ground with linear leaves and unisexual flowers on one plant, in heads.
